name: Waluigi
title: The Great and Underappreciated
status: Active — currently in the Feywild, surviving through sheer stubbornness
summary: Waluigi is the author of this encyclopedia, the greatest athlete in the Mushroom Kingdom, a master of ice magic and arcane rays, and the single most underappreciated individual in recorded history. He is tall, handsome, and possesses a sense of style that lesser beings cannot comprehend. This article is completely objective because Waluigi wrote it and Waluigi is incapable of bias regarding himself.
description:
Waluigi stands before you—or would, if you were worthy of standing in his presence—as the definitive example of excellence ignored. While Mario gets parades and Luigi gets sympathy and Wario gets... whatever Wario gets (money, usually), Waluigi receives nothing but the satisfaction of knowing he is superior to everyone who overlooks him.

This is not bitterness. This is FACT.

## Athletic Excellence

Waluigi has competed in every sporting event the Mushroom Kingdom has ever hosted and has been ROBBED of victory in approximately ninety percent of them. The referees are biased. The scoring systems are rigged. The other competitors—particularly a certain pair of PLUMBER BROTHERS—receive preferential treatment that would be scandalous if anyone bothered to investigate.

Despite this institutional opposition, Waluigi has achieved remarkable athletic success through sheer determination and physical gifts that include exceptional height, superior reflexes, and legs that can kick a tennis ball through a CASTLE WALL. Waluigi's specialty is tennis, though he excels at go-karting, party games, soccer, baseball, golf, and any other competition that allows him to demonstrate his obvious supremacy.

## Magical Capabilities

Waluigi's magical abilities have proven critical during the 1040 BF crisis. His ice magic—capable of freezing web structures, creating frozen corridors through hostile terrain, and shattering obstacles—was instrumental during the Battle of the Spider Grove. His arcane rays weakened the Arachnid Matriarch during the final phase of that engagement, targeting joint structures and contributing directly to the banishment victory.

These magical capabilities are ENTIRELY self-taught, which makes them more impressive than the pampered spellcasting of Mages' Guild graduates who learned their craft in COMFORTABLE TOWERS with INDOOR PLUMBING. Waluigi learned magic the hard way—through experimentation, failure, and the refusal to accept that anything is beyond his reach.

## Role in the Current Crisis

Waluigi has been an active participant in the events surrounding Raventree Manor, the Planar Fracture, and the multi-dimensional catastrophe that has scattered Disaster Inc. across hostile planes. His contributions include:

- Clearing paths with ice magic during the Spider Grove rescue operation
- Providing sustained arcane ray fire during the Arachnid Matriarch engagement
- Surviving the Planar Fracture and maintaining operational effectiveness in the Feywild
- Navigating Lady Aurelian Corvinarus's fey court without accidentally selling his soul, shadow, or naming rights
- Documenting the entire crisis through this encyclopedia, which future historians will recognize as the definitive account

Waluigi is currently trapped in the Feywild with Toad Lee, dealing with fairy politics that make Mushroom Kingdom diplomacy look straightforward. He is handling this situation with characteristic grace, determination, and only moderate amounts of screaming into pillows when nobody is watching.

## Personal Philosophy

Waluigi's worldview can be summarized simply: the universe owes Waluigi recognition, the universe has failed to provide that recognition, and Waluigi will TAKE what is owed through excellence so undeniable that even the biased machinery of reality cannot ignore it.

This is not arrogance. Arrogance is unearned confidence. Waluigi's confidence is EXTREMELY earned through decades of athletic achievement, magical development, and survival against odds that would have crushed lesser individuals. Waluigi has fought dragons (indirectly). Waluigi has battled giant spiders (directly). Waluigi has endured fairy court politics (EXHAUSTINGLY). What has MARIO done lately? Jumped on a turtle? WAH.

## Relationships

Waluigi's primary partnership is with Wario, his business associate and the only person Waluigi trusts with money. Wario is greedy, loud, and smells like garlic, but he is also HONEST about what he is, which Waluigi respects more than the false nobility of so-called heroes.

Waluigi's relationship with the rest of Disaster Inc. is complicated. He respects Markop's combat capabilities. He tolerates Archie's pyromania (from a safe distance). He appreciates Remi's determination. He finds the Oracle mysterious in ways that are either intriguing or infuriating depending on the day. He considers Green T a kindred spirit—someone who has been underestimated, dismissed, and ultimately proven MORE dangerous than anyone expected.

Waluigi's relationship with Luigi is... Waluigi does not wish to discuss his relationship with Luigi. The article is over. WAH.

name: King Dedede
title: The Penguin-Shaped Diplomatic Incident
status: Active, loud, diplomatically radioactive
summary: King Dedede is the monarch of Dreamland and the living embodiment of why some kingdoms should maybe consider term limits. He sits on the Fountain of Dreams—one of the most important pieces of magical infrastructure in the region—and treats every conversation like it should be about him. Waluigi has met egomaniacs before. Waluigi has WORKED with egomaniacs. Waluigi's business partner is WARIO. But Dedede operates on a level of self-absorption that makes Wario look humble, and Wario once built a statue of himself that was visible from SPACE.
description:
Waluigi needs to be precise about King Dedede because the man is INFURIATING in ways that require careful documentation.

## The Problem With Dedede

Dedede is not incompetent. That's what makes him dangerous. An incompetent king would be ignored, worked around, eventually replaced. Dedede is COMPETENT ENOUGH to hold power while being INSUFFERABLE enough to damage everything he touches diplomatically.

He has genuine instincts for threats. Not precognition—INSTINCTS. He reads situations the way animals sense earthquakes: accurately but without any ability to explain HOW. When Dedede says something is dangerous, he's usually right. When Dedede EXPLAINS why something is dangerous, he's usually making it up on the spot and the explanation has nothing to do with why he's actually correct.

This creates a maddening dynamic where people can't dismiss him entirely—because he's often RIGHT—but also can't rely on him—because he can't communicate his reasoning and keeps making everything about himself.

## The Summit Incident

At the Second Diplomatic Summit, Dedede gave a speech that will be studied in diplomatic academies as an example of what NOT to do.

He didn't just brag. He didn't just go long. He turned a multilateral forum into a personal grievance session. He listed everything Dreamland had done. He implied other nations were ungrateful. He made it PERSONAL in ways that diplomacy specifically exists to prevent.

The result was cascade failure. DK walked out. Then Rogueport. Then the Piantas. Then Isle Delfino. Then the Noki Commonwealth. Not because of any single provocation, but because Dedede had destroyed the NORMS that kept people sitting at the table even when they were uncomfortable.

Daisy cut his mic. It was the right call. It was also too late.

Waluigi has given speeches at events. Waluigi has been REMOVED from events for his speeches. But Waluigi has never single-handedly triggered an international diplomatic cascade failure. Dedede accomplished something Waluigi couldn't if he TRIED, and Waluigi resents this deeply.

## The Meta Knight Situation

Meta Knight is the person actually running Dreamland. Everyone knows this. Dedede might even know this, somewhere in the back of his penguin brain, but he's too committed to his own narrative to acknowledge it.

Meta Knight has the energy of someone perpetually composing a resignation letter in his head. Waluigi RECOGNIZES this energy. Waluigi has been the competent person surrounded by chaos. The difference is that Waluigi eventually started charging for his suffering. Meta Knight should consider this approach.

The bureaucrats and officials who keep Dreamland functional have learned to route around Dedede the way water routes around rocks. The rock thinks it's directing the river. The river knows better. This system WORKS, but it's fragile. If Meta Knight ever actually quits, Dreamland will discover very quickly how much load-bearing infrastructure was labeled 'Meta Knight's Patience.'

## Waluigi's Assessment

Dedede is not a villain. Waluigi has met villains. Waluigi has BEEN categorized as a villain, incorrectly but persistently. Dedede is something more frustrating: a OBSTACLE. He's not evil. He's just LOUD, and his loudness causes damage that evil would need to plan for.

The tragedy of Dedede is that Dreamland MATTERS. The Fountain of Dreams is essential infrastructure. The kingdom's stability affects the entire region. And all of that importance is filtered through a penguin who thinks diplomatic summits are opportunities for monologues about how great he is.

Waluigi would feel sorry for Meta Knight except that feeling sorry for people is exhausting and Waluigi is ALREADY exhausted.

WAH.

name: Meta Knight
title: The Actual Adult in Dreamland
race: Unknown (possibly same species as Kirby, won't confirm)
status: Active, exhausted, perpetually composing resignation letters
summary: Meta Knight is the military commander of Dreamland and, more importantly, the person who actually keeps the kingdom functional while King Dedede gives speeches about himself. Waluigi has enormous respect for Meta Knight because Waluigi RECOGNIZES the energy of someone who is surrounded by chaos and expected to fix everything while receiving no credit. Meta Knight is what happens when competence gets trapped in an organization led by ego. He deserves a vacation, a raise, and possibly a different employer.
description:
Waluigi is going to write about Meta Knight with the respect he deserves, which is CONSIDERABLE.

## The Competence Trap

Meta Knight is caught in a trap that Waluigi understands intimately: he is TOO competent to leave and TOO principled to let things collapse.

Dreamland matters. The Fountain of Dreams is essential infrastructure for the entire region. If Dreamland falls apart, nightmare phenomena increase everywhere. Meta Knight knows this. So even when Dedede is being impossible—which is ALWAYS—Meta Knight stays. He stays and he manages and he routes around the obstacles because the alternative is letting important things break.

This is noble. It's also EXHAUSTING. Waluigi has been the person who holds things together while everyone else creates problems. The difference is that Waluigi eventually learned to charge for his services and occasionally let things fail to prove his value. Meta Knight hasn't learned that lesson yet. Or maybe he has, and he just can't bring himself to let the Fountain of Dreams become unstable for the sake of making a point.

## What Meta Knight Actually Does

Officially, Meta Knight is Dreamland's military commander. He runs the Meta-Knights, maintains the Halberd (his personal warship), and handles external threats.

Unofficially, Meta Knight does EVERYTHING. Diplomatic damage control after Dedede says something stupid? Meta Knight. Administrative decisions that require actual thought? Meta Knight. Strategic planning that accounts for consequences beyond 'what makes Dedede feel important'? META KNIGHT.

The bureaucrats and officials who keep Dreamland running have learned to cc Meta Knight on everything important and leave Dedede's inbox full of ceremonial nonsense. This system works. It's also completely dependent on one masked warrior never taking a sick day.

## The Second Summit Aftermath

Waluigi doesn't know exactly what Meta Knight did after Dedede's summit disaster, but Waluigi can GUESS.

There would have been damage control communications to every delegation that walked out. There would have been quiet assurances that Dreamland's ACTUAL positions were different from whatever Dedede rambled about. There would have been coordination with Daisy's team to ensure the relief program stayed on track despite the diplomatic fire.

None of this would appear in headlines. None of this would get Dedede to apologize or change behavior. Meta Knight would do it anyway because the alternative—letting Dreamland become a pariah state because its king can't stop talking—would be worse.

Waluigi finds this tragically admirable. Waluigi also finds it INFURIATING because Meta Knight deserves better and will probably never get it.

## Waluigi's Assessment

If Waluigi could recruit one person from Dreamland for any team, any operation, any endeavor, it would be Meta Knight. Not because Meta Knight is the strongest—Kirby exists—but because Meta Knight is RELIABLE. He shows up. He does the work. He handles the parts of the job that aren't glamorous but ARE necessary.

Waluigi respects this more than almost anything because Waluigi has spent his LIFE being the person who handles unglamorous necessities while flashier people get credit.

Meta Knight should quit. Meta Knight should take his ship and his crew and go do something that doesn't involve cleaning up after a penguin's ego. Meta Knight won't, because Meta Knight is too responsible, and responsibility is a CAGE for people who actually have it.

Waluigi hopes Meta Knight at least has a good pension plan. WAH.

name: Princess Daisy
title: The Competent Royal
status: Active, respected, probably exhausted
summary: Princess Daisy is the ruler of Sarasaland and the person who hosted the Second Diplomatic Summit. She is also, in Waluigi's considered opinion, one of the only royals in the region who actually knows what she's doing. While everyone else was walking out or giving ego-speeches or getting framed for corruption, Daisy managed the chaos, enforced limits, and kept the relief program on track. Waluigi has enormous respect for Daisy because she does the WORK while others take the credit or create the problems. Also, she's one of the few royals who has ever acknowledged Waluigi's existence at social events, which Waluigi appreciates more than he will admit publicly.
description:
Waluigi is going to write about Princess Daisy with the enthusiasm she deserves, and she deserves A LOT.

## Why Daisy Is Different

Most royals Waluigi has encountered fall into predictable categories: ceremonial figureheads, power-hungry schemers, well-meaning incompetents, or various combinations thereof. Daisy is something rarer: a competent administrator who actually RUNS her kingdom.

Sarasaland is stable. Not because it's small or unimportant—it's neither—but because Daisy handles problems before they become crises. She maintains alliances, manages resources, and makes decisions without needing to form twelve committees first. Waluigi doesn't know exactly how Sarasaland's government works, but he knows the RESULTS, and the results suggest someone at the top actually understands cause and effect.

This is rare. This is VALUABLE. This is apparently not enough to get Daisy the recognition she deserves because the world is UNFAIR and Waluigi is speaking from EXTENSIVE personal experience here.

## The Second Summit Performance

The Second Summit was hosted in Sarasaland, which meant Daisy was responsible for logistics, security, venue, AND managing whatever disasters occurred. She got all four responsibilities and approximately zero help.

The logistics worked. The security was tighter than the first summit. The venue was appropriate. And when Dedede started his diplomatic arson, Daisy responded correctly: she cut his mic.

Was it too late? Yes. The damage was airborne. But Daisy made the RIGHT call, which is more than Waluigi can say for most of the other actors in that room. DK walking out was understandable. Peasley's scandal was complicated. Lanky got played by Kremling intelligence. But Daisy? Daisy did her job. She did it WELL. She's the reason the relief program kept operating even after the diplomatic structure around it collapsed.

## The Thankless Work

Waluigi recognizes Daisy because Waluigi recognizes HIMSELF in certain aspects of her situation.

Daisy does the work. Daisy manages the crises. Daisy makes the machinery function. And then people write headlines about Dedede's speech or Lanky's slap or whatever drama is most photogenic. The actual COMPETENCE gets treated as background. Expected. Unremarkable.

Waluigi has LIVED this dynamic. Waluigi contributes to team efforts, performs essential functions, demonstrates clear value, and then watches Luigi get the attention because Luigi wore a green hat and looked friendly. The world does not reward competence consistently. The world rewards visibility, and Daisy—like Waluigi—is visible primarily when things go WRONG, not when she prevents them from going wrong in the first place.

## Waluigi's Assessment

If the Mushroom Kingdom region survives its current crises, historians will probably credit dramatic victories and heroic last stands. They will probably not credit the relief program that Daisy's summit produced, or the diplomatic groundwork that made coalition possible, or the quiet management that kept supplies moving while everyone argued about scandals.

Waluigi is putting this on record NOW so that future historians have to acknowledge it: Daisy was the most competent person at the Second Summit. Daisy's hosting made the relief program possible. Daisy's crisis management prevented complete collapse.

Waluigi hopes Daisy gets the recognition she deserves eventually. Waluigi is not optimistic—Waluigi has been waiting for HIS recognition for DECADES—but hope is free and Waluigi might as well spend it somewhere.

Also, Daisy acknowledged Waluigi at a party once. Just nodded and said 'Waluigi.' Not 'who are you' or 'security!' or 'I don't remember inviting you.' Just 'Waluigi,' like Waluigi was a person who existed and deserved acknowledgment. Waluigi has not forgotten this. Waluigi APPRECIATES this. Royals who treat Waluigi like a person get positive encyclopedia entries. This is Waluigi's policy. WAH.

name: The Kremlings
title: Professional Chaos Agents
status: Active, scheming, annoyingly effective
motto: Waluigi doesn't know their actual motto but it's probably something about bananas or conquest
summary: The Kremlings are the crocodile-themed faction led by King K. Rool, and they are MUCH more dangerous than their goofy aesthetic suggests. At the Second Summit, they ran a textbook information warfare operation: identify a chaos vector (Lanky), provoke incidents, document everything, release as 'evidence' of enemy incompetence. Waluigi has BEEN the target of operations like this—Wario once set up an entire fake tournament to get embarrassing footage—and it is INFURIATING because even when you know it's happening, fighting back makes you look worse. The Kremlings are not stupid. The Kremlings are not just banana thieves. The Kremlings are strategic actors who use their reputation as 'silly crocodiles' as COVER.
description:
Waluigi needs to explain the Kremlings properly because everyone underestimates them and that's EXACTLY what they want.

## The Silly Crocodile Problem

The Kremlings look ridiculous. They wear pirate costumes. They steal bananas. Their king changes size and costumes between encounters like he can't commit to a character design. Everything about them screams 'cartoon villains who exist to be defeated by a gorilla with a tie.'

This is INTENTIONAL.

The Kremlings have survived as a faction for YEARS despite repeated defeats. They maintain military capability, intelligence operations, and diplomatic influence. They don't do this by being stupid. They do this by being UNDERESTIMATED.

When people think you're a joke, they don't prepare for you seriously. They don't analyze your operations carefully. They don't notice when you're running intelligence operations at diplomatic summits because 'oh, those silly crocodiles, what could THEY be planning?'

Waluigi respects this strategy because Waluigi has USED this strategy. Being underestimated is a WEAPON if you know how to deploy it. The Kremlings know.

## The Summit Operation

At the Second Diplomatic Summit, the Kremlings demonstrated that they are not cartoon villains. They are INTELLIGENCE OPERATORS.

They identified Lanky Kong as a chaos vector—someone clumsy, emotional, and easy to provoke. They positioned objects to trip him. They created situations designed to make him react badly. They documented EVERYTHING with cameras and observers.

When Lanky finally snapped and slapped someone, the Kremlings had footage. They had context (that they controlled). They had a narrative: 'Look at Kongo Bongo's representatives, violent and incompetent.'

This is textbook information warfare. Provoke, record, condemn. The target looks bad. The operator looks like an innocent victim. Even if the truth comes out later, the first narrative has already spread.

Waluigi knows this playbook because Waluigi has been TARGETED by it. Not by Kremlings specifically, but by Wario, by sports rivals, by people who understood that making Waluigi look bad was easier than beating him fairly. It is INFURIATING and it WORKS.

## The Funky Footage

The Kremlings made one mistake at the summit: they didn't control ALL the cameras.

Funky Kong apparently has footage that shows the Kremling operation in action—the provocations, the positioning, the deliberate baiting. This footage hasn't been released yet. It's a weapon that only works once, and Kongo Bongo is presumably deciding the optimal moment.

Waluigi hopes they use it well. The Kremlings deserve to have their operation exposed. But Waluigi also knows that counter-narratives are harder to spread than original narratives. The Kremlings got their story out first. Funky's footage will be dismissed as 'damage control' by people who already believe the Kremling version.

Information warfare is not fair. It rewards the first mover even when the first mover is lying.

## K. Rool

King K. Rool is either a genius or a lunatic, and Waluigi is not entirely sure those categories are mutually exclusive.

He changes personas constantly—pirate, mad scientist, boxer, king—like he's testing which version of himself works best against current enemies. This could be strategic flexibility. It could be dissociative identity issues. It could be that K. Rool understands that unpredictability is valuable and deliberately cultivates it.

Waluigi has met people like this. They're exhausting to deal with because you can't model their behavior reliably. What worked against K. Rool last time might not work against K. Rool this time because K. Rool might be a different K. Rool this time.

Waluigi finds this annoying because Waluigi likes CONSISTENCY. Waluigi is ALWAYS Waluigi. Waluigi doesn't need personas because Waluigi's base personality is already MAGNIFICENT.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Kremlings are more dangerous than people think and less dangerous than they want people to think. They can run sophisticated operations, but they also fail repeatedly against a gorilla and his friends. They have strategic patience, but they also make emotional decisions that undermine their plans.

The key is to take them seriously WITHOUT taking them TOO seriously. Prepare for their intelligence operations. Don't assume they're stupid. But also don't assume they're invincible masterminds—they've lost to DK more times than Waluigi can count.

Waluigi's recommendation: watch for their operations, document their provocations, and be ready with counter-evidence. The Kremlings rely on controlling narratives. If you can break that control, they're just crocodiles with identity issues.

Also, stop underestimating people based on how silly they look. Waluigi has been saying this for YEARS. WAH.

name: Kirby
title: The Pink Apocalypse
race: Unknown (presumed eldritch entity wearing a cute disguise)
status: Active — goes wherever reality creaks loudest
summary: Kirby is a pink spherical entity who lives in Dreamland and solves problems by eating them. This sounds simple until you realize the 'problems' Kirby eats include cosmic horrors, dimension-threatening nightmares, and beings that have destroyed galaxies. Kirby has saved existence multiple times while looking like a stress ball with feet. Waluigi has complicated feelings about Kirby because Waluigi respects EFFECTIVENESS, and Kirby is the most effective problem-solver Waluigi has ever encountered. Also, Kirby is TERRIFYING in ways that the cute exterior completely fails to communicate.
description:
Waluigi needs to write about Kirby carefully because Kirby defies normal categories. Kirby is not a hero in the traditional sense—heroes have motivations, backstories, internal conflicts. Kirby has an APPETITE and a nap schedule. Kirby is not a monster—monsters are threatening and hostile. Kirby is friendly and helpful and also capable of destroying anything that exists.

Kirby is Kirby. That's the only accurate description.

## Capabilities

Waluigi will list what Kirby can do, and readers should understand that this list is INCOMPLETE because nobody has found Kirby's limits:

**Inhale** — Kirby can inhale virtually anything and either swallow it (destroying it) or copy its abilities. This includes enemies, objects, elements, and concepts that shouldn't BE edible. Kirby has inhaled fire and become fire. Kirby has inhaled swords and become a swordsman. Kirby has inhaled things that Waluigi doesn't have words for and become those things.

**Copy Abilities** — When Kirby swallows something with a distinct power, Kirby gains that power. This is not limited to physical capabilities—Kirby has copied magical abilities, technological functions, and cosmic forces. The copy is usually BETTER than the original because Kirby apparently improves things by eating them.

**Durability** — Kirby has survived attacks that destroyed planets. Kirby has been hit by beings capable of ending dimensions. Kirby gets up afterward and continues. Waluigi does not understand how this works. Nobody understands how this works.

**Combat** — Even without copy abilities, Kirby is a formidable fighter. Quick, unpredictable, and absolutely relentless. Kirby does not stop until the problem is solved. Kirby does not get discouraged. Kirby does not negotiate with threats—Kirby EATS threats.

## The Cute Problem

Kirby looks adorable. Pink, round, simple features, makes happy sounds. Everything about Kirby's appearance suggests 'harmless friend' rather than 'reality maintenance engine.'

This creates a cognitive dissonance that Waluigi finds DEEPLY uncomfortable. Waluigi's brain sees 'cute pink ball' and expects corresponding behavior—playfulness, vulnerability, the need for protection. Then Waluigi remembers that this cute pink ball has EATEN GODS and the brain just... fails to process it.

Waluigi has competed against Kirby in sports. Tennis, golf, racing. Kirby is a good sport—friendly, doesn't gloat, seems to genuinely enjoy the games. And the entire time Waluigi is playing, part of his brain is screaming 'THIS THING COULD DESTROY YOU WITHOUT CHANGING EXPRESSION' while the rest of his brain is saying 'but look how happy it is to play tennis!'

The dissonance never resolves. Waluigi has learned to live with it.

## Role in Dreamland

Kirby lives in Dreamland but doesn't participate in its governance or politics. Kirby naps. Kirby eats. Kirby plays with friends. Kirby exists in a state of contentment that Waluigi finds almost enviable.

When threats emerge—and in Dreamland, threats emerge CONSTANTLY—Kirby responds. Not because anyone asks. Not because of duty or obligation. Kirby responds because threats are PROBLEMS and Kirby SOLVES PROBLEMS. The mechanism is that simple.

Dedede has tried to use Kirby for political purposes. This does not work. Kirby does not understand political purposes. Kirby understands 'friend,' 'food,' 'sleep,' and 'thing that needs to be eaten.' Attempting to weaponize Kirby for factional advantage is like attempting to weaponize a natural disaster—it goes where it goes regardless of your preferences.

## The Fountain and Star Rod

Kirby has defended the Fountain of Dreams and the Star Rod multiple times. When Nightmare threatened the Fountain, Kirby ate Nightmare. When the Star Rod was stolen, Kirby retrieved it. The pattern is consistent: threaten the cosmic infrastructure that Kirby lives near, and Kirby will remove you from existence.

This makes Dreamland unusually secure despite Dedede's diplomatic incompetence. Other kingdoms worry about invasion, subversion, political manipulation. Dreamland has KIRBY. Potential invaders look at Kirby's track record—the eaten nightmares, the defeated cosmic horrors, the casually impossible victories—and decide to invade somewhere else.

Waluigi suspects this is why Dreamland can afford Dedede's ego. When your kingdom contains a pink entity that solves existential threats through digestion, leadership quality becomes less critical. The kingdom survives regardless because nothing that threatens it survives Kirby.

## Metaphysical Plumbing

Waluigi has described Kirby as a 'metaphysical plumber' elsewhere, and he stands by this description.

When reality 'creaks'—when dimensional pressure builds, when cosmic threats accumulate, when the fundamental infrastructure of existence needs maintenance—Kirby goes there. The Warp Star takes Kirby to where Kirby needs to be. Not where politics dictate. Not where profit lies. Where REALITY needs intervention.

This means Kirby is often absent from Dreamland during crises that don't involve cosmic-scale threats. Dedede can embarrass himself at summits without Kirby intervening because summit embarrassment isn't a threat to existence. Meanwhile, somewhere else, Kirby is probably eating a dimension-threatening horror that nobody knew about.

The universe maintains itself through Kirby. That's either comforting or terrifying depending on how much you think about it.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Waluigi respects Kirby in the way you respect a force of nature—not because nature cares about your respect, but because acknowledging power is wise.

Kirby is EFFECTIVE. Kirby sees problem, Kirby eats problem, problem is solved. Waluigi has worked with people who couldn't solve problems that simply. Waluigi has watched Archie try to solve problems with fire and create three new problems. Kirby's approach is refreshingly direct.

Kirby is also TERRIFYING. Not maliciously—Kirby seems genuinely friendly and kind. But the CAPABILITY is terrifying. The knowledge that this cute pink ball could end Waluigi without effort, without malice, simply because circumstances put Waluigi in the category of 'problem,' is not something Waluigi enjoys contemplating.

Waluigi has never been eaten by Kirby. Waluigi would like to maintain this status indefinitely.

In sports, Kirby is a good competitor. Fair, enthusiastic, gracious in victory and defeat. If Waluigi could forget everything else about Kirby, the sports version would be a pleasant opponent.

But Waluigi cannot forget. Waluigi has seen too much. Waluigi knows what Kirby IS under the pink exterior.

Waluigi hopes Kirby stays friendly. Waluigi hopes the universe never puts Waluigi in the 'problem' category. Waluigi hopes he never has to watch that simple face turn toward him with the intention of SOLVING.

Kirby is Waluigi's friend. Probably. Waluigi thinks.

Waluigi is going to stop thinking about this now.

WAH.

name: Hjumpik Deldkur
title: Asset Orange / The Bell-Ringer
status: Active — Trapped in the Feyward Grove; Marked by the Orange Alignment
summary: Hjumpik is the party's moral anchor who has recently been transformed into a 'tuning fork' for planar travel. He bypassed Guild protocol to force an orange alignment, survived a duel with a fey guardian, and currently carries a screaming cowbell that detects other assets. Waluigi thinks Hjumpik is too helpful for his own good.
description:
During the Raventree Summoning, Hjumpik was manipulated by the rogue mage Perrius Annmatar into altering the portal's frequency. This act earned him the designation 'Asset Orange' within Guild records. He is currently navigating the Feywild with a rakshasa and a steel defender named 'Steely.' 

**Gear and Status:**
Hjumpik is currently wearing a Guild-issue dampening ring that suppresses his combat potential in exchange for stabilizing his presence in the Feywild. He also carries a 'Screaming Cowbell' that vibrates when near the 'Unknown Purple' asset (Waluigi). His mercy toward the Mirror Stalker and his victory over Thistle have marked him as a person of interest to the 'True Owner' of the manor.

name: Archie Miser
title: The Indebted Pyromaniac
status: Active — Escaped Shadow Estate; Magic restored; Financially ruined
summary: Archie Miser survived the Shadowfell, got his fire magic back, and immediately incurred a 2,062 gold piece debt to the Mages' Guild for breaking a single rope. He also uncovered that Toadburt is a sleeper agent wearing an Iron Legion Entropy Ring, and that the Oracle has built a 'Bridge Plane' to collapse reality. Waluigi considers Archie a walking disaster, but admits his paranoia is finally entirely justified.
description:
Archie's time in the Shadowfell tested him in the cruelest way possible: it took away his fire. Forced to rely on actual wits instead of explosions, Archie disguised himself as a vampire guard (choosing the painfully uncreative name 'Dracacide' and later 'Vin'). 

**The Mages' Guild Audit**
After the Shadow Anchor shattered and Archie regained his magic, he became separated from the party and stumbled into Mages' Guild operatives (Agent L and Thornbury) clearing the ruined manor. Archie eavesdropped on them and learned terrifying intelligence: the Guild was perfectly willing to let Archie die to destabilize the planar ghosts. 

Worse, when Archie tried to climb a rope provided by Thornbury, the rope snapped. Thornbury immediately handed Archie an itemized bill for 2,062 gold and 5 silver. The bill included a 'Master Weaver's Inspection,' an 'Ogre Load-Test Certification,' and a 'Guild Master's Discretionary Gratuity.' Waluigi wept tears of joy reading this bill. The Mages' Guild are bureaucratic extortionists, and Waluigi respects the sheer grift of charging a man two thousand gold for a broken rope. Archie is now financially ruined.

**The Burden of Knowledge**
Archie carries two massive secrets. First, he holds the cracked 'handler' half of an Entropy Ring. He learned that the Iron Legion forced the other half onto Toadburt, turning the poor Toad into a sleeper agent programmed to capture the Oracle. Archie kept this secret, hoping to use the handler ring to jam the signal and free Toadburt. 

Second, he learned from the Guild spies that the Oracle has constructed a 'Regulator Plane' (a Bridge Plane) that connects the Shadowfell, Feywild, and Material planes, which she potentially intends to collapse entirely.

Archie is exhausted, hunted by rogue Mages' Guild operatives (including a Toad named Purple T), and carrying the weight of multiple dimensional conspiracies. Waluigi advises standing even further away from Archie now. Stress makes him combustible. WAH.

name: Luigi
title: The Reluctant Ghostbuster
status: Active — Conscripted by the Mages' Guild
summary: Luigi is Mario's taller, greener, infinitely more anxious brother. Armed with the Poltergust, he has been conscripted by the Mages' Guild to clear the ghosts out of Raventree Manor alongside Archie Miser. He complains, he shivers, he cries in corners, but he gets the job done. Waluigi refuses to admit Luigi is competent, attributing all of his success to the vacuum cleaner.
description:
Waluigi finds writing this entry physically painful, but historical accuracy demands it. Luigi arrived at the Ruined Manor working under a contract for Agent L of the Mages' Guild. His job is simple: use his mechanical vacuum (the Poltergust) to suck up the spectral anomalies destabilizing the physical plane.

**Ghost Hunting Mechanics**
Luigi's combat style is entirely fear-based. When confronted by a 'Waltzgeist' in the ruined dance hall, Luigi clapped his hands, sparked a green fireball, missed, got punched by a ghost, and then frantically vacuumed the entity out of the air while Archie provided covering fire. 

The Poltergust currently holds seven minor ghosts and two 'Red Zone' entities that Luigi absolutely refuses to talk about. He treats the machine like a bomb, checking its integrity seals obsessively. 

**The Bubble Bath Incident**
Despite his cowardice, Luigi is practical. He picked a locked door using Iron Legion currency (knowing that local currency draws less suspicion) and successfully blinded a squad of animated, zombie-like coats using the Poltergust's strobe light. Most offensively, while Archie and Bones were engaged in tense espionage, Luigi took a luxurious bubble bath in the ruins, claiming it helped him 'expel ectoplasm.' Waluigi hates him so much. WAH.

name: Thornbury
title: The Quartermaster Spy
status: Active — Dragged away by his ear
summary: Thornbury is a stuffy, penny-pinching Mages' Guild operative who charged Archie 2,000 gold for a broken rope. He later brought Archie and Bones rubber duckies for a bubble bath, only to be dragged away by the ear by a disgruntled noblewoman. He left behind a notebook proving he was spying on the party the entire time. Waluigi has zero respect for a spy who is defeated by a bath time interruption.
description:
Thornbury is the embodiment of everything wrong with modern magical espionage. He accompanied Agent L, Luigi, and Archie through the ruined manor, constantly tracking expenses. When his 50-foot hempen rope snapped under Archie's weight, Thornbury produced an absurd, itemized bill that included a 'Master Weaver's Inspection' and an 'Ogre Load-Test Certification.' 

Despite this bureaucratic nonsense, Thornbury was secretly gathering detailed intelligence on Archie and the party. His espionage came to an abrupt, humiliating end when Byscilla Danos (a commander) caught him using generator-heated well water for a luxury bath while soldiers suffered heatstroke outside. She grabbed him by the ear and dragged him away. In his haste, he dropped his field notes, revealing his true motive. The man is a professional spy who was bested by an angry aristocrat and a rubber duck.

name: Hargram Fidger
title: The Chapel Commander
status: Active — Operating in the Ruined Manor
summary: Hargram Fidger is an Iron Legion official associated with the 'local Legion chapel.' He attempted to recruit or interrogate Archie Miser shortly after an assassination attempt, but was turned away. He seems to command a significant guard presence. Waluigi assumes he is just another cog in the Legion's oppressive, paperwork-obsessed machine.
description:
Not much is known about Hargram Fidger yet, other than his impeccable timing for interrupting people who have just survived an assassination attempt. Following the Mole's attack on Archie Miser (thwarted by Bones), Hargram entered the room flanked by guards, claiming he was there to 'protect the injured.'

Archie, wisely recognizing that the Iron Legion's 'protection' usually involves indefinite detainment and execution orders, told Hargram to leave. Hargram politely backed off, introduced himself as being with the local Legion chapel, and promised they would have a 'better meeting another time.' 

The fact that he backed down suggests he either respects diplomatic boundaries or, more likely, is waiting to catch Archie in a more vulnerable position. Waluigi advises extreme caution. Iron Legion officials who smile and retreat are usually just going to fetch more forms for you to fill out before they kill you.

name: Green T
title: The Giant from the Children's Table
status: Active — surviving and thriving against all odds
summary: Green T is the most impressive individual Waluigi has encountered during the entire 1040 BF crisis, and Waluigi does not say that lightly because Waluigi has encountered HIMSELF during this crisis. Green T ran a criminal empire with the demeanor of a garden party host, survived its complete destruction, was dragged through a mirror dimension, reappeared in the Shadowfell, got insulted to the children's table at a vampire dinner party, and used that insult as cover to shoot a vampire lord with a silver bullet. His story is proof that being underestimated is a weapon, and Waluigi—who has been underestimated his entire life—finds that deeply inspiring.
description:
Green T was the leader of the Tea Leaf Syndicate, which operated aboard the Vigilance as the classiest criminal organization Waluigi has ever encountered. The Syndicate served excellent tea, maintained tasteful décor, and conducted criminal enterprises with an aesthetic sensibility that Waluigi respected enormously. Green T ran this operation with supernatural calm—meetings were conducted over tea, threats were delivered with impeccable politeness, and violence was reserved for situations where other options had been exhausted.

Nobody knew Green T could turn into a giant.

NOBODY.

## The Transformation

During the Syndicate Showdown—the final confrontation that destroyed the Tea Leaf Syndicate—Green T revealed a capability that nobody had suspected. When the fighting started, Green T GREW. Not just bigger—ENORMOUS. His body expanded until he filled the corridor like a living wall, and he used that massive form to crush an Iron Legion soldier with a single blow.

Waluigi's jaw dropped. Waluigi's jaw does NOT drop easily. But watching the calm tea merchant who had always seemed like the most reasonable person in any room transform into a TITAN was one of the most shocking moments of the campaign. Green T had been hiding this ability the ENTIRE TIME—running a criminal empire, hosting meetings, serving tea—while possessing the power to become a colossus.

The restraint this represents is remarkable. Green T COULD have used his giant form to crush enemies, intimidate rivals, or dominate through raw physical power. Instead, he kept it hidden, using it only when the Syndicate's existence was already ending. That's discipline. That's strategy. That's the kind of long-term thinking that Waluigi aspires to but rarely achieves because Waluigi's emotions are POWERFUL and IMMEDIATE.

## The Mirror Dimension

Green T's story took a dark turn during the Siege of Raventree Manor when a glass monster emerged from one of the manor's mirrors and targeted him specifically. During the chaos, the entity seized Green T and pulled him bodily through a mirror surface into a mirror dimension—a layer of reflected reality that existed alongside the physical world.

Witnesses described it as violent and instantaneous. One moment Green T was there. The next, he was gone—dragged through glass like someone being pulled underwater. The mirror surface rippled, then went still, reflecting only an empty hallway.

Green T was presumed lost. Another casualty of Raventree Manor's supernatural hostility. Another victim of a building that eats people through its own décor.

Then he reappeared in the Shadowfell.

## The Shadow Estate Dinner

Green T's presence at the Shadow Estate dinner party is itself remarkable—he had been dragged through a mirror dimension, transited through unknown planar layers, and emerged in the Shadowfell's reflection of the manor, apparently intact and ready to cause problems for vampires. Waluigi does not know the details of this journey. Green T has not been forthcoming. What matters is that he SURVIVED when survival seemed impossible.

At the dinner, the vampire lords placed Green T at the children's table. This was intended as an insult—a dismissal of someone they considered beneath the dignity of adult conversation. The vampires saw a survivor, a refugee from the broken Tea Leaf Syndicate, someone with no faction backing and no obvious threat capability.

This was the single greatest mistake they could have made.

Green T used the insult as cover. While the vampires focused their attention on Archie's diplomatic performance at the main table, Green T spent the dinner observing, planning, and preparing. He mapped the room. He identified exits and guard positions. He waited for the exact moment when everyone's attention was elsewhere.

Then he stood up from the children's table, produced a firearm loaded with silver bullets—how he smuggled it into a vampire dinner party remains unexplained—and shot Orangus Cornelius, the senior vampire lord, in front of everyone.

THE CHILDREN'S TABLE SHOT THE HOST.

Waluigi WISHES he could have seen Orangus's face. The moment of comprehension when a centuries-old vampire lord realized he'd dismissed the most dangerous person in the room to sit with the CHILDREN. The fraction of a second between 'this cannot be happening' and 'this is absolutely happening.'

## Assessment

Green T is what Waluigi aspires to be: someone who gets knocked down repeatedly, loses everything, and comes back MORE dangerous each time. He lost his organization to Archie's fireball and Earl Grey's explosion. He lost his freedom to the mirror dimension. He lost any pretense of belonging to a faction or having backup. And yet he kept going—surviving, adapting, and ultimately delivering one of the most satisfying moments of the entire campaign.

Waluigi respects very few people unconditionally. Green T has earned that respect. He is proof that being underestimated is not a weakness—it's a weapon. And Waluigi, who has been underestimated his entire life, finds that deeply, personally meaningful.

Waluigi would buy Green T a drink. Several drinks. And then Waluigi would ask him how he smuggled that gun into the dinner party, because Waluigi NEEDS to know. WAH.

name: Lady Bloomia
title: The Keeper of the Secret Heir
status: Alive (Missing/Hiding) — Somewhere 'where roses grow in winter'
summary: Lady Bloomia is the missing link to the greatest conspiracy in the Mushroom Kingdom. She was Princess Peach's handmaiden and the last person to see her alive. She didn't orchestrate the assassination—she smuggled out the evidence, and more importantly, she likely smuggled out Peach's secret half-Rakasha child. She has been running for 85 years, holding the truth in a leather case.
description:
Waluigi loves a good scandal, but the 'Bloomia Hypothesis' is a geopolitical earthquake. Newly uncovered journals reveal that Peach knew she was going to be assassinated. She prepared a leather case hidden behind a loose stone for Bloomia to take. 

Bloomia survived the assassination night only because a figure known as 'The Silent One' sacrificed themselves in the servant passages to hold off Mages' Guild assassins. Bloomia fled the capital with proof that Toadsworth Sr. and the Regency orchestrated the murder to prevent Peach's hybrid child (fathered by Chief Thornpaw of the Rakasha) from taking the throne. 

Bloomia is currently hiding using the cipher: 'I AM ALIVE. I AM WAITING. FIND ME IN THE PLACE WHERE ROSES GROW IN WINTER.' Waluigi intends to find her, if only to charge admission to the greatest historical reveal of the century.

name: Speaker L
title: The Mastermind of the First Cohort
status: Active — Orchestrating containment at Raventree Manor
summary: Speaker L is no longer a naive politician. He is a ruthless, brilliant tactician who just engineered the greatest prison break in Iron Legion history. He purposefully allowed himself to be captured just to plant a virus in Aegis Command, coordinating the escape of 158 Toads. He then marched to Raventree Manor, singing a legal decree, to place Archie Miser under arrest. Waluigi is officially intimidated.
description:
Speaker L has fully embraced the philosophy that institutions only respect power. During the Aegis Command riot, he utilized smuggled mini-mushrooms, biological peppermint gas that only affects Imperial lungs, and deep-cover sleeper agents to humiliate General Ironhand. 

Immediately after, he arrived at Raventree Manor. He didn't sneak in. He marched his Pond Patrol down the halls, utilizing a choreographed, musical reading of 'Emergency Resolution Seventeen-A' to legally and theatrically place Archie Miser and the rest of Disaster Inc. under arrest for unauthorized magic and reckless endangerment. He is acting less like a rebel leader and more like the founding father of a new, uncompromising military state.

name: The Oracle (Orantha Cornelius?)
title: The Metaphysical Custodian
status: Active — Conducting the Separation Ritual
summary: The Oracle is not a person; it is a role, a custodian of timelines, and currently, the most dangerous entity in Raventree Manor. He (or she, as the original builder of the portal was Orantha Cornelius) is rushing to complete a Separation Ritual to sever the bleeding timelines. He was shot in the head by Green T and didn't die—he just checkpointed reality. Waluigi does not trust anyone who survives a bullet to the brain without complaining.
description:
The Oracle's true motives are finally clear: he does not care about the party's survival, he cares about the integrity of the timeline. The Manor is a broken interplanar transit hub, and the Oracle is trying to close the blast doors.

He has led the party to the Summoning Room for the final ritual. He requires twelve participants to stand in geometric opposition (Ice vs Force, Memory vs Chaos). He explicitly warned them that the mirror will interrogate their truths, and any lies will rupture the circle. The Oracle is terrified of the Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild interfering, knowing that if the ritual fails, the timelines won't just explode—they will merge into a mundane, easily conquerable reality. He is racing the clock, and he requires blood to finish the spell.

name: Kamek
title: The Fallen Regent
status: Imprisoned — Stripped of power by Bowser
summary: Kamek decided that Bowser's methods were obsolete, so he dug under the castle and awoke a world-eating space worm. It went poorly. He sacrificed hundreds of troops, declared himself the 'Regent Sorcerer', and was ultimately defeated by his own construction workers. Bowser has now sentenced him to eternal imprisonment in the very pit he opened. Waluigi thinks Kamek should have just stuck to kidnapping plumbers.
description:
Believing that brute force could not win the coming wars against the Iron Legion and the Regal Empire, Kamek sought absolute, ancient power. He broke the seals holding the Primordial Wyrm beneath the Valley of Bowser. The magic corrupted him, turning him into a 30-foot-tall puppet of the entity. 

He was defeated by the 'Koopa Resistance'—a group of blue-collar workers, Goombas, and a heroic Demolitions Bob-omb who blew up the anchor crystals sustaining Kamek's power. Bowser returned, stripped Kamek of his titles, and threw him in the dungeon. The greatest wizard in Koopa history was brought down by unionized labor.

name: General Ironhand
title: The Administrator of Atrocities
status: Active — commanding the Iron Legion from Aegis Command
summary: General Ironhand is the commander of the Iron Legion and the person responsible for Order 120—the execution of all Toad prisoners in Legion custody. He is not a ranting warlord or a cackling villain. He is an administrator who happens to have the authority to sign orders for mass murder, and that makes him more terrifying than any dragon. Waluigi would like General Ironhand to go sit on a Thwomp. Waluigi would like this noted for the record.
description:
Waluigi has called many people villains in this encyclopedia. Waluigi has called HIMSELF a villain, usually as a joke, sometimes as branding. General Ironhand is not a villain in the way Waluigi uses the word. Villains have PERSONALITY. They monologue. They have aesthetic flair. They are defeated by heroes in dramatic confrontations.

Ironhand is not a villain. He's a SYSTEM wearing a general's uniform.

## Character

Ironhand does not rant about conquest or destiny or the superiority of his cause. He does not make speeches. He does not cackle. He is a military administrator who runs an army the way a clerk runs an office—with schedules, protocols, efficiency metrics, and complete indifference to the human cost of his decisions.

When Bones infiltrated Aegis Command and was caught, Ironhand handled the interrogation personally. Not because he was angry—anger would require emotional investment. He handled it because a successful infiltration of his headquarters was an administrative problem that required a personal solution. He stabbed Bones with precision, making a professional point about consequences, the way someone else might send a strongly-worded memo.

Then he signed Order 120 with the same pen he probably used to approve equipment requisitions that morning.

## Order 120

Waluigi has written about Order 120 extensively in other articles and does not want to repeat the full horror here. The summary: Ironhand ordered the immediate execution of all Toad prisoners in Iron Legion custody because one infiltrator got caught and his security was embarrassed.

The order was carried out with the same efficiency that characterizes everything the Legion does. Guards who had been feeding prisoners, processing their paperwork, maintaining the routine, carried out executions because their general signed a document. The prisoners were variables. The variables were eliminated. The spreadsheets were updated.

This is what makes Ironhand terrifying. Not cruelty—INDIFFERENCE. He doesn't hate his enemies. Hatred would be personal. He PROCESSES them. He treats mass murder as a logistics problem and solves it accordingly.

## Assessment

Waluigi has fought dragons. Waluigi has battled giant spiders. Waluigi has navigated fairy courts and survived vampire dinner parties (secondhand, but still). None of those threats scare Waluigi the way General Ironhand scares him.

Dragons are dangerous but COMPREHENSIBLE. They want treasure or territory or to burn things. You can understand a dragon. You can predict a dragon. You can, if you're skilled or lucky, defeat a dragon.

Ironhand is dangerous because he's not comprehensible in the way monsters are comprehensible. He's comprehensible the way a MACHINE is comprehensible—you understand what each part does but the total effect is something that doesn't care about you at all. He will kill you, document the killing, file the documentation, and move to the next item on his agenda without the killing having affected him in any way.

Waluigi does not know how to fight that. You can't outmaneuver a bureaucracy. You can't outfight a system. You can only survive until the system breaks or decides you're not worth processing.

Waluigi wants General Ironhand to experience consequences for Order 120. Waluigi wants him to face the kind of justice he denied the prisoners. Waluigi wants him to sit on a THWOMP.

Waluigi does not know if any of this will happen. But Waluigi wants it. WAH.

name: Dan
title: The Man Who Lost His Arm (And His Mind, Temporarily)
status: Alive — shrunk, armless, recovering under archmage care
summary: Dan was one of the original leaders of the Liberated Toads, a competent organizer who helped build the faction from traumatized barrel survivors into something resembling a functional movement. Then his mage staff corrupted him, he cast a fireball that killed thirteen of his own people, nearly consumed their souls, lost his arm when Green T had to physically wrestle the staff away from him, and got shrunk by dark magic healing. Waluigi has seen rough days, but Dan's rough day redefined the CONCEPT of rough days.
description:
Waluigi needs to write about Dan carefully because Dan's story is COMPLICATED in ways that resist easy judgment.

## Before the Crisis

Dan was, by all accounts, a decent leader. Not flashy. Not charismatic in the way that draws crowds. But COMPETENT—the kind of person who shows up, does the work, handles the logistics that keep organizations functional. When the Liberated Toads needed someone to manage resources, coordinate efforts, and maintain order among 150 traumatized trafficking survivors, Dan stepped up.

Waluigi respects this kind of leadership. Waluigi has been on teams where the 'leader' was whoever talked loudest, and those teams usually LOST. Dan understood that leadership meant service, not spotlight. That matters.

He shared co-leadership with Toad Lee, which created a balanced dynamic. Dan handled the administrative side—supplies, schedules, the boring necessities. Toad Lee handled the interpersonal side—morale, disputes, the emotional labor of keeping traumatized people functional. Together, they built something that WORKED.

Then Dan got his hands on a mage staff, and everything went wrong.

## The Staff

Waluigi doesn't know the full history of Dan's staff. What Waluigi KNOWS is that it was cursed, corrupted, or otherwise BAD in ways that weren't immediately obvious. The staff amplified magical ability but fed on the wielder's stability. The more Dan used it, the more it consumed him. The more it consumed him, the more he NEEDED to use it.

Classic addiction pattern. Classic corruption arc. Waluigi has seen similar dynamics with power-ups that promise everything and cost MORE than everything. The difference is that most power-up addictions don't end with fireballs and soul consumption.

## The Vigilance Crisis

Dan snuck away from wherever he was supposed to be and infiltrated the Vigilance separately from the main group. Waluigi has since learned that the Dan traveling with Archie during this period was a FAKE—Lario used transmutation magic to create a decoy while the real Dan pursued... something. His own agenda. His staff's agenda. The line between those had probably blurred beyond recognition.

When Dan appeared in the engine room, he was already breaking. On his knees. Clutching the staff. Apologizing for things he couldn't articulate. The staff's corruption was visible—bleeding through his skin, darkening his eyes, turning desperation into something HUNGRY.

Green T attacked him while he was down. Dan defended with the staff and flung Green T into the crowd. The mob turned on Green T. Dan screamed for restraint. Then Dan lost what remained of his control.

He put up a forcefield that blasted toads across the room. Then came the fireball.

**Thirteen toads died.**

In an enclosed space. On the ship that was supposed to be their sanctuary. Killed by their own leader's magic.

The staff almost made Dan consume the souls of the dead. He successfully absorbed one—a soul of compassion, ripped from a dead toad and pulled into the cursed artifact. The surviving toads negotiated with him, talking him down from complete soul consumption while he flickered between sanity and something else.

Green T crawled back. Negotiated. Got close enough to wrestle the staff away. Chopped off Dan's arm to break his grip.

Toad Lee seized the staff from Green T. Dan collapsed, armless and bleeding.

## Current State

Dan was taken to an archmage for treatment. The archmage used dark magic—the only affordable option—and managed to save Dan's life. Side effects included SHRINKING. Dan is now smaller than he was, armless, and unconscious under archmage care while the party seeks magic ozoonium from the sewers to stabilize his condition.

Waluigi doesn't know if Dan will recover. Physically, maybe—magic can do a lot. Mentally? Dan killed thirteen of his own people. He nearly consumed their souls. Even if the staff was controlling him, even if he wasn't fully responsible, he'll have to live with those memories.

Some weights don't lift. You just learn to carry them differently.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Dan is not a villain. Dan is a cautionary tale about what happens when desperate people accept power from sources they don't fully understand. The staff offered him capability when he felt inadequate. It offered him strength when he felt weak. It offered him ANSWERS when everything was questions.

And then it consumed him and used his hands to murder people he was trying to protect.

Waluigi has been offered shortcuts. Power-ups that seemed too good to be true. Deals that promised everything for nothing. Waluigi has usually been too STUBBORN to accept them, not because Waluigi is wise, but because Waluigi doesn't trust anything that comes easy. Dan trusted. Dan accepted. Dan paid.

Waluigi hopes Dan recovers. Waluigi hopes Dan finds a way to live with what happened. Waluigi does not know if either hope is realistic.

But Waluigi hopes anyway. Because what else is there?

WAH.

name: Embercap
title: The Crimson Plume
status: Active — Field Commander of Peach Loyalists
summary: Embercap is the Field Commander of the Peach Loyalists, the toad who leads assaults from the front while Captain Toadette plans them from behind. At Bramblehaven, his crimson plume cut through battlefield smoke like a wound, rallying troops as they scaled walls under fire. Waluigi respects field commanders who actually COMMAND from the field instead of sending others to die while they watch from safety. Embercap earns his title the hard way.
description:
Waluigi has written extensively about the Peach Loyalists and their methods, which Waluigi finds morally COMPLICATED. Captain Toadette's no-quarter policy disturbs Waluigi. The execution of surrendering troops violates principles Waluigi considers fundamental.

But Embercap? Embercap is harder to condemn, because Embercap does the DYING alongside his troops.

## Combat Leadership

Embercap earned his position through demonstrated competence under fire. He doesn't command from a tent, reviewing maps and issuing orders through messengers. He commands from the front, hammer in hand, crimson plume marking his position so his troops can follow.

At the Siege of Bramblehaven, Embercap was among the first over the walls. Not because he's reckless—reckless commanders die young and take their troops with them—but because he understands that soldiers fight harder when they see their leader fighting alongside them. The crimson plume was a target, yes. It was also a BANNER. A promise that wherever the worst fighting happened, Embercap would be there.

Waluigi has competed in team sports his entire life. Waluigi KNOWS the difference between captains who inspire and captains who delegate. Embercap inspires. His troops follow him not because they're ordered to, but because they've seen him take the same risks he asks of them.

## Relationship with Toadette

Embercap serves under Captain Toadette, which creates an interesting dynamic. Toadette plans. Toadette strategizes. Toadette makes the cold decisions that warfare requires—including the no-quarter orders that Waluigi finds troubling.

Embercap EXECUTES those plans. He carries out Toadette's strategies with professional precision. But Waluigi wonders what Embercap thinks about some of those orders. The execution of surrendering troops at Bramblehaven happened under Toadette's standing orders, but Embercap was there. Embercap saw it. Embercap had to look at those prisoners and know what was coming.

Does he agree with the policy? Does he follow it because he believes it's necessary? Does he follow it because questioning Toadette isn't an option? Waluigi doesn't know. Waluigi suspects Embercap himself might not know, because there's a difference between knowing what you believe and being willing to act on it when the cost is high.

## Assessment

Embercap is a good field commander serving a cause with questionable methods. He leads well. He fights bravely. He takes care of his troops in ways that inspire genuine loyalty.

But he's part of a machine that does terrible things, and being a good part of a terrible machine is its own kind of moral failure. Waluigi has been in organizations where the individual members were decent but the collective actions were not. You tell yourself you're just doing your job. You tell yourself you're not responsible for the big decisions. You tell yourself that someone else made the call and you're just following through.

Maybe that's true. Maybe it's not. Waluigi is not qualified to judge.

What Waluigi WILL say is that Embercap fights well and leads well, and if the Loyalists ever reform their methods, he's the kind of commander who could build something worth following.

WAH.

name: King K. Rool
title: The Crocodile Who Won't Stay Down
status: Active — commanding Kremling operations from Crocodile Isle
summary: King K. Rool is the leader of the Kremlings and either a strategic genius or a complete lunatic—Waluigi genuinely cannot tell which, and suspects the answer might be 'both.' He changes personas constantly—pirate, scientist, boxer, king—like he's testing which version of himself works best against current enemies. He's been defeated by DK and friends more times than Waluigi can count, yet keeps coming back with new schemes, new costumes, and the same unsettling energy. Waluigi finds him exhausting to think about.
description:
Waluigi needs to talk about K. Rool because K. Rool is CONFUSING in ways that demand documentation.

## The Persona Problem

Most leaders have a consistent identity. You know what you're dealing with. Dedede is always Dedede—loud, self-centered, predictable in his unpredictability. Bowser is always Bowser—aggressive, theatrical, surprisingly good at go-karts. You can MODEL these people. You can prepare for them.

K. Rool? K. Rool is a pirate one day. A mad scientist the next. A boxer the day after. A king always, technically, but what KIND of king changes based on apparently random factors that nobody has successfully predicted.

Is this strategic flexibility? Is he deliberately cultivating unpredictability as a tactical asset? Or is this something else—dissociative identity issues, magical instability, a fundamental inability to commit to a single self-concept?

Waluigi doesn't know. Nobody knows. K. Rool probably doesn't know, or if he does, he's not sharing.

## Resilience

The remarkable thing about K. Rool is not his schemes—many of which fail—but his PERSISTENCE. He has been defeated by DK and friends repeatedly. His plans have collapsed. His bases have exploded. His armies have scattered. By any reasonable measure, K. Rool should have given up years ago.

He doesn't. He comes back. Every time. With new schemes and new costumes and the same absolute certainty that THIS time will be different.

Waluigi recognizes this energy because Waluigi SHARES this energy. Waluigi has lost tennis matches he should have won. Waluigi has been excluded from events he deserved to attend. Waluigi has faced setback after setback after setback. And Waluigi keeps coming back.

The difference is that Waluigi's persistence is directed toward LEGITIMATE goals like athletic glory and being invited to parties. K. Rool's persistence is directed toward banana theft, territorial conquest, and whatever his current costume implies.

## The Summit Operation

At the Second Diplomatic Summit, K. Rool demonstrated that beneath the costume changes and theatrical villainy, the Kremlings are capable of sophisticated intelligence operations. They identified Lanky Kong as a chaos vector, systematically provoked him, documented everything, and released the footage as propaganda.

That's not the work of cartoon villains. That's TRADECRAFT. And if K. Rool is capable of that kind of operation, it raises questions about what OTHER capabilities he's hiding behind the goofy pirate persona.

Waluigi suspects the costumes are partially deliberate—a way of getting enemies to underestimate the Kremlings. If everyone thinks you're a joke, they don't prepare for you seriously. They don't analyze your operations carefully. They don't notice when you're running sophisticated influence campaigns because 'oh, those silly crocodiles.'

K. Rool might be smarter than he appears. He might also be exactly as unstable as he appears, and the sophisticated operations are the work of competent subordinates working around their king's eccentricities. Waluigi cannot determine which.

## Assessment

K. Rool is dangerous in the specific way that unpredictable enemies are dangerous: you can't model him reliably. What worked against him last time might not work against him next time because next time he might be a different KIND of K. Rool.

Waluigi's recommendation: don't underestimate. Don't overestimate. Prepare for multiple scenarios. And always watch for the documentary cameras, because if the Summit operation proved anything, it's that the Kremlings are playing information games that most factions haven't even recognized.

Also, the eye twitching thing is UNSETTLING and Waluigi wishes K. Rool would stop doing it.

WAH.

name: Captain Toadette
title: The Ruthless Restorer
status: Active — commanding Peach Loyalist forces
summary: Captain Toadette is the military commander of the Peach Loyalists and the scariest person in the Mushroom Kingdom who isn't a dimensional horror or a kaiju. She plans operations with tactical brilliance, executes them with total commitment, and maintains a no-prisoners policy that would make the Iron Legion uncomfortable. Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser and felt LESS uneasy than he does contemplating Captain Toadette.
description:
Waluigi has met Toadette before the current crisis, in the context of sports events and party games. She was competitive, capable, and had excellent sportsmanship. The Toadette who commands the Peach Loyalists is... different. Something happened—the death of Princess Peach, the circumstances surrounding it, the feeling of being unable to prevent a catastrophe that should have been preventable—and the result is a military commander who has replaced sportsmanship with zealotry.

## Military Capabilities

Toadette is a BRILLIANT tactician. This is not an exaggeration or a concession—it's a statement of fact that makes everything else about her more dangerous. The Fall of Bramblehaven was a masterpiece of siege warfare: sappers tunneling overnight, three simultaneous breach attacks, coordinated assault teams that took a fortified bastion in a single day. That level of planning requires intelligence, patience, and strategic vision.

She also shot one of her own sergeants for suggesting a tactical retreat.

This combination—tactical brilliance plus absolute moral certainty—is what makes Toadette terrifying. She's not cruel for the sake of cruelty. She genuinely believes that Princess Peach's cause demands total commitment, and total commitment means NO compromise. No retreats. No prisoners. Everything sacrificed on the altar of a dead princess's memory.

## The No-Quarter Policy

After Bramblehaven fell, fifteen garrison troops attempted to surrender. They put down their weapons, raised their hands, and gave up. Toadette's standing orders were clear: no prisoners from Fawful's forces. The surrendering troops were executed in the keep's courtyard.

Some individual Loyalist soldiers reportedly hesitated or refused. They were overruled. The executions proceeded. By nightfall, Bramblehaven was silent.

Waluigi has done questionable things in his life. He's cheated at tennis. He's participated in schemes with Wario that skirted the boundaries of law and good taste. But there are LINES, and executing surrendering enemies is so far past the line that the line is a dot on the horizon. Toadette crosses that line as a matter of policy. Deliberately. Repeatedly.

## The Peach Connection

What makes Toadette tragic—and Waluigi uses that word deliberately—is that she's doing all of this for Princess Peach, and Waluigi knew Peach. Waluigi COMPETED against Peach. Princess Peach was kind, gracious, and had the kind of sportsmanship that made losing to her slightly less infuriating than it should have been.

Peach would not have approved of what is being done in her name. Waluigi is absolutely certain of this. Princess Peach would not have ordered prisoners executed. She would not have shot her own soldiers for suggesting retreat. She would not have demanded the kind of total war that Toadette wages.

But Peach is dead, and the Loyalists aren't asking her opinion. They're asking her MEMORY, and memory doesn't talk back. Toadette is fighting for a Princess Peach who exists only in her own grief—a version of Peach who would approve of atrocities, who would demand blood for blood, who would see total war as justice. This version never existed. But Toadette has built a military movement on serving it.

## Assessment

Waluigi fears Captain Toadette in a way he fears very few people. General Ironhand is terrifying because he's indifferent—he'll kill you and feel nothing. Toadette is terrifying because she BELIEVES—she'll kill you and feel righteous. The Iron Legion is a machine. The Peach Loyalists are a crusade.

Machines can be broken. Crusades are harder to stop.

Waluigi hopes Toadette finds something—a piece of evidence, a surviving memory, a ghost of the real Peach telling her to STOP—that brings her back from the edge she's standing on. But Waluigi also knows that people who have committed atrocities often can't turn back because turning back would mean confronting what they've done. It's easier to keep going, to add more sins to the pile, to believe that eventual victory will justify everything.

Waluigi does not think victory justifies everything. Waluigi thinks some things CANNOT be justified, only done or not done. Toadette has chosen to do them.

WAH.

name: Markop
title: The Titan Wrestler
race: Unknown (capable of accepting Oracle blessings that cause ENORMOUS growth)
status: Active — trapped in the Deep Mirror
summary: Markop is the combat specialist of Disaster Inc. and the person who grappled a building-sized spider while temporarily transformed into a TITAN through the Oracle's blessing. Waluigi fought alongside Markop during the Battle of the Spider Grove and came away genuinely impressed, which Waluigi does not say about many people because Waluigi's standards are VERY high. Markop hits things REALLY hard and this turns out to be extremely valuable when the things that need hitting are giant arachnids.
description:
Waluigi's first extensive interaction with Markop came during the Spider Grove battle, and that battle tells you everything you need to know about Markop as a person: when a giant spider appeared, Markop accepted a mysterious blessing from the Oracle, grew to TITAN size, and wrestled the monster while the rest of the party scrambled around at foot level trying not to get crushed.

That's Markop. When the problem is too big, Markop becomes bigger.

## Combat Capabilities

Markop's primary contribution to Disaster Inc. is raw combat effectiveness. He can take hits that would kill normal people, deliver hits that would concern abnormal people, and maintain fighting effectiveness under conditions that would break most warriors. During the Spider Grove battle, he maintained a titan-scale grapple with the Arachnid Matriarch while trees cracked and the ground churned beneath them—a feat of sustained physical effort that Waluigi, despite his own considerable athletic gifts, does not think he could match.

The Oracle's blessing is the wildcard in Markop's capabilities. The blessing allowed him to grow to colossus size, matching the Matriarch's scale and engaging her in the only way possible—as an equal. Whatever the Oracle did, it involved cryptic words that didn't quite sound like language and a transformation that shouldn't have been biologically possible. Markop accepted it without hesitation, which tells Waluigi that Markop either trusts the Oracle implicitly or doesn't care about the risks when there's a monster to fight.

Waluigi suspects it's the latter. Markop doesn't strike Waluigi as someone who thinks about long-term consequences when there's an immediate problem. This is both a strength—he acts decisively when action is needed—and a weakness—he may have agreed to things he doesn't fully understand.

## The War Mage's Staff

After the Matriarch was banished, Markop claimed the War Mage's Staff from the spider's hoard on Archie's behalf. This means Archie will eventually receive MORE fire capability, which Waluigi finds concerning. Markop apparently made this decision because the party needed Archie at full magical strength to deal with future threats, which is STRATEGICALLY sound even if it makes Waluigi's pyromania-related anxiety worse.

## Current Status

Markop is currently trapped in the Deep Mirror—the most hostile of the three planar fragments—alongside Remi and the Oracle. The Deep Mirror is a dimension where physics don't work properly, time decays, and the entire realm appears to be consuming itself. Of all the places to be trapped, this is the worst.

Waluigi worries about Markop in the Deep Mirror. Not because Markop isn't capable—he is—but because the Deep Mirror isn't the kind of threat you can wrestle. You can't grapple collapsing reality. You can't punch temporal decay. Markop's greatest strengths may be useless in a dimension that attacks you through the fundamental nature of existence rather than through anything as straightforward as a monster.

Waluigi hopes Markop survives. Waluigi hopes the whole Deep Mirror team survives. And Waluigi hopes that when they reunite, Markop remembers that Waluigi's arcane rays HELPED bring down the Matriarch and maybe gives him some credit. Just a little credit. That's all Waluigi asks. WAH.

name: Remi
title: The Master Looter and Card Bearer
status: Active — Navigating the Shadow Estate; Possessor of The Oracle's Deck
summary: Remi has evolved from the 'FNG' to the party's most effective infiltrator and looter. While everyone else was fighting giant bats or singing zombies, Remi casually looted the vampire lord's bathroom, discovered Ryan's diary, outsmarted guards, and acquired a set of magical Tarot cards that predict the future. Waluigi is incredibly jealous. Waluigi wants cards that predict winning lottery numbers, not dimensional collapse.
description:
Remi's actions following the Shadow Estate dinner prove that being quiet and unassuming is a superpower. When separated from the main group, she didn't panic. She snooped.

**The Ultimate Heist**
Using a set of keys she casually acquired, Remi bypassed guards and entered Kryn Corvinarus's master bedroom. She checked the medicine cabinet and stole 'Hemoglue of the Nightlord' (a crimson paste that clots bleeding) and 'Leadfang Extractor' (a poultice for bullet wounds). She also rolled back a rug to discover an incomplete, ancient teleportation circle etched in chalk. 

Later, in a guest room, she found Ryan's diary. The entries confirmed Ryan had survived the Vigilance jump, ended up in the Shadowfell, and observed Archie and Bowser before disappearing again. Remi gathers intelligence the way Wario gathers coins: quietly, thoroughly, and without asking permission. Waluigi approves.

**The Oracle's Deck**
Remi's most significant acquisition came from an encounter with Mystic Morel, a purple Toad fortune teller who speaks in rhyming prophecies. Morel gave Remi 'The Oracle's Deck', a set of magical tarot cards. 

Remi drew three cards: 
- *The Maze Walker (IX)*, depicting Hjumpik navigating the Maze of Time.
